title: Ever Patient, Loving, Meek
description: Ever Patient, Loving, Meek in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 120, “The Mind Which Was in Christ Jesus”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ev-er pa-tient, lov-ing, meek, Ho-ly Sa-viour, was thy mind; Vain-ly in my-self I seek Like-ness to my Lord to find; Yet the mind that was in thee May be, must be, formed in me.

lines: Likeness to my Lord to find;
Yet the mind that was in thee
May be, must be, formed in me.
Since such griefs were thine to bear,
For each sufferer thou couldst feel,
Saviour, let thy grace in me
Form that mind which was in thee.
When my pain is most intense,
Let thy cross my lesson prove;
Let me hear thee even thence;
Breathing words of peace and love;
Thus thy grace shall form in me
The same mind which was in thee.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
